prompt: Bags of trail mix have weights that are approximately normal with mean $250$ grams. About $16$ percent of the bags weigh LESS than $244$ grams. What is the standard deviation, in grams?
hint: You know the mean, one value and the area below it. An area can be matched to a $z$-score, and a $z$-score links the value to the standard deviation.

hints.text: You know the mean, one value and the area below it. An area can be matched to a $z$-score, and a $z$-score links the value to the standard deviation.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: if $2.5$ percent of bags were below $240$ grams, that is $z = -2$, so two SDs $= 10$ grams and the SD is $5$. Same move with 16 percent.
An area of $0.16$ to the left matches $z \approx -1$ by the empirical rule. Set $\frac{244 - 250}{\sigma} = -1$ and solve for $\sigma$.
$\frac{-6}{\sigma} = -1$ gives $\sigma = 6$, so the standard deviation is $6$ grams.

explanation: By the empirical rule, about $16$ percent of a normal distribution lies more than one standard deviation below the mean, so $244$ grams is at $z \approx -1$.
Write the $z$-score formula with the unknown standard deviation: $-1 = \frac{244 - 250}{\sigma} = \frac{-6}{\sigma}$.
Solving gives $\sigma = 6$ grams. (Using invNorm$(0.16) = -0.994$ gives $\sigma = 6.03$, the same to the nearest gram.)

alternativeExplanations.title: Think in distances
steps: The gap between the mean and 244 grams is 6 grams.
That gap is one SD wide, because 16 percent sits below it.

alternativeExplanations.title: The trap: using 34 percent
steps: The 34 percent in the empirical rule is the area between the mean and one SD below, not the tail.
The TAIL below $z = -1$ is $50 - 34 = 16$ percent, and the problem gave 16 percent, so $z = -1$ is right.
Match the given area to the right picture before reading off $z$.
